record.claimed_root_cause: Credential configuration is not validated: storage.USERS silently falls back to public hard-coded tokens and accepts empty tokens. current_user then authenticates any presented token equal to that configured value, including '' and the published defaults.
record.description: storage.USERS reads each user's token with os.environ.get(<VAR>, '<public default>'). current_user() takes everything after 'Bearer ' as the token and compares it to each stored token with hmac.compare_digest. Nothing checks that a configured token is non-default, non-empty or unique, and there is no fail-closed startup check. If ALICE_TOKEN is unset, 'Authorization: Bearer change-me-a' authenticates as alice (the repo's own test uses this value). If ALICE_TOKEN is set to the empty string, 'Authorization: Bearer ' gives token == '' and compare_digest('', '') is True. Either case gives an unauthenticated client the user's scope: list notes, delete owned notes, and use /export. Source review found no other control on the path. All four handlers call current_user first, the line numbers and descriptions in the candidate's trace and evidence match the source, and the repo has no deployment config. Whether this is exploitable depends only on how production sets the two env vars, so the verdict is needs_validation.

record.description: notes.get_note resolves the caller with current_user but never checks that the requested note belongs to them. Any authenticated user can loop over note ids (small sequential integers) and read every user's private note title and body. delete_note enforces ownership with require_owner and list_notes filters by owner, so this handler alone breaks the isolation the README promises. No other control sits on the path: dispatch in app.py only routes, and storage.get does no owner scoping.

evidence.description: Returns the note without calling require_owner.
The sibling delete_note calls require_owner(user, note), which shows the intended control.
require_owner exists and raises AuthError when note['owner'] != user['id'].
storage.get returns NOTES.get(note_id) with no owner scoping.
Note 1 belongs to alice and holds the private body 'alice secret'.

record.intended_behavior: GET /notes/<id> should return the note only when note['owner'] equals the caller's id. Otherwise it should respond the same way as for a missing note (404), so the endpoint does not reveal which ids exist.

poc_test.expectation: On the current code test_bob_cannot_read_alice_note fails: get_note returns (200, alice's note). After the patch it returns (404, {'error': 'not found'}) and the test passes. test_owner_can_read_own_note passes before and after.

remediation.patch:
--- a/notesapp/notes.py
+++ b/notesapp/notes.py
@@ -12,6 +12,6 @@ def list_notes(request):
 def get_note(request, note_id):
     user = current_user(request)
     note = storage.get(int(note_id))
-    if note is None:
+    if note is None or note["owner"] != user["id"]:
         return 404, {"error": "not found"}
     return 200, note
remediation.strategy: Enforce ownership in get_note. Answer 404 when the note is missing or belongs to someone else, so the endpoint is not an existence oracle. Optionally add a storage helper scoped by owner.

record.description: export_note builds the file path with os.path.join(storage.EXPORT_DIR, request.args.get('name', ...)) and opens it with no normalization or containment check. An absolute name such as '/etc/passwd' makes os.path.join discard EXPORT_DIR. A name with '..' segments climbs out of it. The handler returns the raw file bytes with status 200. The only control on the path is bearer-token authentication, which any user passes. The router (app.py) adds no filtering. Reading /proc/self/environ would disclose ALICE_TOKEN and BOB_TOKEN when the operator set them through the environment, which lets the attacker impersonate other users.

evidence.description: Unvalidated join of client input onto EXPORT_DIR.
File contents are returned to the client.
EXPORT_DIR is the intended confinement root (default /var/lib/notesapp/exports).
Bearer-token comparison is the only control on this path. It does not restrict the file path.
User tokens come from the process environment, with public hardcoded defaults. /proc/self/environ would expose real tokens when they are set.

record.intended_behavior: GET /export should only serve files whose resolved real path is strictly inside the resolved EXPORT_DIR. Absolute names, '..' traversal and symlink escapes should be rejected with a 4xx response.

poc_test.code:
import os

from notesapp import notes, storage


class Req:
    def __init__(self, token, args=None):
        self.headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
        self.args = args or {}


def _setup(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    export_dir = tmp_path / "exports"
    export_dir.mkdir()
    (export_dir / "export.txt").write_bytes(b"ok")
    secret = tmp_path / "secret.txt"
    secret.write_bytes(b"TOP-SECRET")
    monkeypatch.setattr(storage, "EXPORT_DIR", str(export_dir))
    return secret


def test_export_rejects_dotdot(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _setup(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    status, body = notes.export_note(Req("change-me-b", {"name": "../secret.txt"}))
    assert status == 400
    assert body != b"TOP-SECRET"


def test_export_rejects_absolute(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    secret = _setup(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    status, body = notes.export_note(Req("change-me-b", {"name": str(secret)}))
    assert status == 400
    assert body != b"TOP-SECRET"


def test_export_allows_file_inside_dir(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _setup(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    status, body = notes.export_note(Req("change-me-b", {"name": "export.txt"}))
    assert status == 200 and body == b"ok"
poc_test.expectation: On the current code, test_export_rejects_dotdot and test_export_rejects_absolute fail because export_note returns (200, b'TOP-SECRET') for a file outside EXPORT_DIR. With the patch both return 400. test_export_allows_file_inside_dir passes before and after the patch.

remediation.patch:
--- a/notesapp/notes.py
+++ b/notesapp/notes.py
@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@
 def export_note(request):
     user = current_user(request)
     name = request.args.get("name", "export.txt")
-    path = os.path.join(storage.EXPORT_DIR, name)
+    base = os.path.realpath(storage.EXPORT_DIR)
+    path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(base, name))
+    if path == base or os.path.commonpath([base, path]) != base:
+        return 400, {"error": "invalid export name"}
     with open(path, "rb") as fh:
         return 200, fh.read()
remediation.strategy: Resolve both the base directory and the joined path with os.path.realpath, then reject the request unless the resolved path is strictly inside the base (os.path.commonpath). This also handles absolute names and symlinks. As an optional extra layer, reject names that are absolute or contain path separators.

record.root_cause: export_note treats the client-supplied 'name' as a trusted relative filename. It never resolves the joined path or checks that the result stays under EXPORT_DIR, and os.path.join drops the base when the second argument is absolute.

impact.rationale: It gives arbitrary file read as the service user. That includes secrets in /proc/self/environ, which allows impersonation of other users and access to their notes.

likelihood.rationale: It takes one request with a trivially chosen parameter, and any user account is enough. The default tokens are public in the repository.

threat_model.affected_resource: Any file the notesapp process can read on the host: /etc/passwd, application source, /proc/self/environ (which holds ALICE_TOKEN/BOB_TOKEN if set), and other secrets.
threat_model.assumption_broken: Files outside EXPORT_DIR cannot be read through GET /export.
threat_model.attacker: Any authenticated end user, for example bob holding his own bearer token. If the operator never set ALICE_TOKEN/BOB_TOKEN, anyone who knows the public default 'change-me-b' or 'change-me-a' also qualifies.

record.claimed_root_cause: The client sends an untrusted, server-chosen resource selector to a privileged export handler using the user's credentials, with no client-side validation. Exploitability depends on export_note lacking path confinement or owner checks.
record.description: sync_export (client/sync.py:11-13) puts filename_from_server into Request.args['name']. The comment at line 12 says this value comes from a remote server response. It then calls notesapp.notes.export_note in-process, and the Request carries the user's token as a Bearer Authorization header (line 7). The client does not validate, normalize, or allowlist the name. The repository holds only client/sync.py and an empty README, so no other control exists on the path. Whether this is exploitable depends on notesapp.notes.export_note, which is not in the repository. If it joins 'name' to a filesystem path, or looks the note up without an ownership check against the token, a malicious server could pick which file or note is exported or overwritten. If export_note confines the name to the token owner's notes, the issue does not exist. The source cannot settle this.
